body:
It's hard to tell because the [HTML call HTTP redirect-fetch](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigating-across-documents:http-redirect-fetch) sends a `request` and a `response`, while [the definition of HTTP redirect-fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-http-redirect-fetch) accepts a `fetch params` and a `response`. 

`fetch params` lasts throughout the whole redirect chain, and so does its `fetch controller`.

So I think actually this PR does it correctly, but we can only tell for sure once we correct the call to HTTP redirect-fetch mismatch.

body:
It's not needed because fetch would already report timing for these cases internally.

Unfortunately the current behavior is a cross-origin violation as per https://github.com/w3c/resource-timing/issues/340. Adding a resource timing entry for 204/network-errors in lieu of a `load` event exposes that information about a cross-origin-no-TAO iframe.
